newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China prepares budget for HK post-97 leader.
newsitem.headline: China prepares budget for HK post-97 leader.

text.p: A senior Chinese official said Hong Kong's future leader, to be named on Wednesday, will be happy with a budget that Britain and China are working out for the year straddling the territory's 1997 return to Chinese rule.

Chen Zuo'er, a Chinese representative at diplomatic negotiations on the transition budget, said the chief executive-designate and his team would be pleased with the budget that is now in the making, Hong Kong radio reported.
Chen was speaking after experts from the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group held their latest round of budget talks on Tuesday.
He called on the British colonial administration not to make major changes in the Hong Kong government's revenue policy after the two-day talks, the radio said.
Treasury Secretary Kwong Ki-chi, who led the British team, said the two sides would meet early next year for more talks.

Details of the budget have not been revealed. "We are now into the phase where we are discussing the revenue aspect of the budget... We are confident we will reach consensus on the budget which will be in the long-term interest of Hong Kong and which will be conducive to a smooth transition," Kwong told reporters.

The British colony returns to China's control at midnight next June 30. China has pledged to give Hong Kong a high degree of autonomy and preserve its capitalist way of life for 50 years after the handover.
